resources.string: The Home switch starts and stops VPN. The start or refresh icon at the top of every page starts VPN or restarts it with saved settings. Tap the subscription header to open Subscriptions; an empty library opens the import form.

Grant system VPN consent on first start. Choose Rule, Global or Direct routing and system, gVisor, mips or mixed TUN stack (default mips). Restart from the top bar to apply saved routing, stack or runtime changes. Home theme changes apply immediately. With very large text, swipe the stack row sideways to reach all options.

Running appears only after the core confirms TUN is ready. Another VPN taking over, a system disconnect or an externally disabled TUN stops Jeemi and updates the controls; an unexpected core exit shows Service error. Returning to the app checks the current session without reclaiming VPN; start it explicitly when needed. Restart closes the old tunnel first and interrupts active connections; unsaved drafts are not applied. Notification refusal does not block an authorized VPN. Core outbound traffic is protected against routing loops.
View the mihomo version and architecture included in this package.
The manual Check button runs only the version command to diagnose installation or architecture issues.
Android runs the installed executable. Update the app package to update the core. Normal startup does not repeat the version check.
Inject Home runtime preferences as the final layer after subscription and local processing.

Basic and DNS scalar values always override the composed source, including false. Optional resources use an injection switch and Append unique / Override segments. Mapping append merges by key, with the whole Home value winning for a duplicate key.
Disabling an optional resource preserves its source value rather than writing false or an empty list. Saving keeps the source document and current session unchanged.
Show selectors from the composed candidate and live nodes and latency from the matching session.

The collapsed subscription panel shows expiry date, usage and time since refresh. Expand it to select a highlighted subscription card, refresh it, or link a local config or script. Tap the panel header to collapse it. Selectors show their chosen node on the right. A valid HTTP/HTTPS image in the final group icon field takes priority; while loading or if unavailable, the leading emoji in the name is used, then the default group icon. Use a plain image URL, not a Markdown link. Use the lower toolbar to test, search, show hidden groups or configure unmatched traffic. Search keeps node selection and latency tests available. Tap a regular node latency badge to test it. Nested groups use the same two-line card and show the current final node latency; tapping that badge only opens the child group. Return paths appear only inside child groups, and headers show only the final node name; green is up to 200ms, yellow up to 500ms, red is slower or failed. Individual tests pause during batch testing.

Search node names using | for OR, & for AND and ! to exclude. Full-width ｜ ＆ ！ from mobile keyboards work the same way. Apply OR first, then all AND terms, then exclusions. For example, hk | jp & gm !ev requires hk or jp, also gm, and excludes ev. Matching ignores case and whitespace around each term, including full-width spaces; internal spaces remain literal. Selector names, protocols and provider names are not searched. Batch tests use only the results; no matches never falls back to all nodes. Without a matching active session, manual selectors save a preferred node for the next start. Members loaded only from remote providers become available after startup. Automatic groups still select their own nodes. Latency tests require a matching active session; old session data is never presented as a new result. A failed refresh download retries once directly while Jeemi VPN is still running. This does not change routing mode or restart VPN; failure keeps the saved subscription.
Manage rule providers from the composed candidate, including disabled entries.
Disable a provider and its referencing rules, or refresh an HTTP provider in the matching running session.
Enable states are saved per subscription and applied before unmatched-traffic and Home overrides. Restart the active session after changes.
Subscription cards provide Script, Config and Chain shortcuts. Tap a name to change its binding; use the action on the right to bind or unbind.

Scripts and configurations are mutually exclusive: choosing the other kind replaces the current handler. Multiple chain groups can be linked independently. Configurations reference groups and rule sets through routing plans.

Check and preview leaves bindings unchanged. Saving validates resources, affected candidates and core configuration; failures retain old bindings. Unbinding affects only that category on that card, keeps shared resources and the selected subscription, and takes effect on restart.
Read the candidate produced by the current configuration or script operation.
Inspect the complete saved subscription composition, or test a resource draft before saving it.
This view shows a composed candidate. Reference checks do not replace device connection tests. Exports contain the full configuration and may contain credentials.
Read the stored original or normalized subscription document.
Compare imported content with its mihomo representation when diagnosing conversion issues.
These views and exports may contain credentials. Opening a document neither fetches an update nor applies it to a running core.
Process subscriptions using field enable states, composition strategies and a local routing plan.

Edit fields, apply them to the draft, then save for associated subscriptions. The bundled App routing rules configuration rebuilds rules and selectors while retaining node sources, with MATCH using 🚀 Proxy selector. In Rule mode, while its three rule sets are empty, traffic uses that selector except for higher-priority rules such as Home LAN bypass.

Home preferences and the subscription fallback override still apply last. The preset matches Block, Direct, then Proxy; restart after adding rules. To identify apps starting with empty rules, set Home process lookup to always. Bundled resources are added once, remain editable and deletable, and are never associated automatically. Applying field drafts and saving are separate; disabled fields are not injected.
Run a local JavaScript main(config) function that returns a configuration object.
Transform a subscription when field overrides cannot express the required changes.
Preview executes the draft locally using the selected subscription. Scripts have a two-second deadline, a 256 KiB limit and no network or file APIs. Saving alone does not execute a VPN.
Create a logical rule group or a group that emits a mihomo proxy selector.
Rule groups select proxy, direct or reject behavior. Selectors filter nodes and configure health checks. Enter one name pattern per line; prefix ! excludes matches.

Group category is fixed after creation. Each rule set belongs to one group. Inline output requires local rule sets. Reference order affects priority. Include all subscription proxy providers lets the running core load every remote node source. It cannot be combined with name/protocol filters; clear them before enabling it. Preview does not download provider nodes.

Create reusable local or HTTP rule sets for strategy groups. Local classical sets default to App list, showing app details and labels for other rules. Turn it off for text editing only. See the App list help for details.

Local content uses complete payload YAML. For an empty rule set, enter only payload: and the backend treats it as an empty list; payload: [] also works. For nonempty sets, enter one rule per line. Classical example:

payload:
  - PROCESS-NAME,com.example.app
  - DOMAIN-SUFFIX,example.com

Adding from connection details generates a block list automatically. Domain entries contain only domain patterns; ipcidr entries contain only CIDR ranges. Remote sources specify URL, behavior, format and update interval.

Empty sets keep their references but emit no provider or matching rule. Only an omitted payload value is treated as an empty list; explicit null, ~, empty - items and a missing payload field are still rejected. Enter match conditions only, without DIRECT, REJECT or a selector name; the owning group determines the outbound. Source changes retain both drafts until saving validates the selected source. MRS requires domain or ipcidr. No-resolve does not change rule order.

Build a sparse local override with the mihomo field tree. A switch controls whether a field is injected, independently of its value: an enabled false still overrides the source with false. A disabled field leaves the source unchanged.

Search field names or help descriptions. Click a parent name to expand it and a leaf name to edit its typed value and merge strategy. Parent switches only affect already configured editable descendants, even when filtered; a dash means partial selection. Only enabled retains ancestor paths. Show locked additionally reveals read-only fields managed by Home, Android or the routing plan.

Disabling retains the value and strategy; editing a value does not enable it. Locked fields have no editable local value, and optional Home resources follow their own injection switch rather than always replacing the source. The tree describes the supported catalog, not a live session or every protocol-specific option. Applying changes only updates the draft; save the resource and restart an active VPN to apply them.
This area is reserved for connection, log and diagnostic tools.
Future diagnostics will be available through this navigation entry.
Tools are deferred in this version. Current work covers Home, Subscriptions and Config.
